question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a Core-owned Pi/Review/squash-promotion orchestration subsystem, or require this workflow to live in an owner plugin or external platform service using the existing TaskFlow seam?
rationale: The answer sets a durable Core-versus-owner boundary and supply-chain ownership model; it cannot be safely inferred from tests or mechanical code review.

options.title: Keep it outside Core
options.body: Require a narrower owner-plugin or external-service implementation built on generic TaskFlow facilities, without naming Pi, Review, or promotion policy in Core.

options.title: Sponsor a generic Core seam
options.body: Define the minimal service-agnostic Core API and migration/ownership contract before accepting any orchestration implementation.

recommendation.title: Keep it outside Core
recommendation.body: Require a narrower owner-plugin or external-service implementation built on generic TaskFlow facilities, without naming Pi, Review, or promotion policy in Core.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository direction already addresses the same Core-versus-plugin multi-agent ownership boundary.
